transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hello. Um... well, I suppose I'm here because... I'm having some trouble with my thoughts lately. 

I just keep getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that I've missed something critical. Like at work—I deal with data—I'll suddenly think I left a wrong number in a release. Or just things at home, like an unlocked back door, or paying a bill from the wrong account. 

And... well, even when I know I already checked it, my mind just won't let go of the possibility that I've caused some sort of disaster. So... I guess that's why I'm here.

When you have these troubling thoughts, do you find yourself doing certain things over and over—like checking, counting, or repeating actions—to try to ease the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Um... yes. I do. Mostly just to... calm myself down, I suppose. 

I'll end up reopening the spreadsheets. Or rereading emails, just... line by line. And the other things... checking the locks, or looking at the payment confirmations. I just... I kind of have to do it in a set order. Over and over, until it finally feels safe. 

It's... well. Some nights I'm still just sitting at my desk hours later, and... I haven't actually finished anything.

latest_inference.note: The patient's description of intrusive, recurring thoughts followed by repetitive behaviors performed in a specific order to alleviate anxiety strongly points toward OCD (F42.9). The symptoms do not align with generalized anxiety disorder (F41.1) or major depressive disorder (F32.9) based on the current dialogue.
